title: Marriage Act Amendment (Recognition of Foreign Marriages for Same-Sex Couples) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would recognise in Australia same-sex marriages validly solemnised overseas by changing the Marriage Act 1961's rules on recognition of foreign marriages.
It would remove the existing prohibition and expressly recognise overseas marriages between two men or two women under the proposed replacement provision.
Couples in those marriages would have the same Commonwealth rights and obligations as opposite-sex married couples, with the amendments beginning on Royal Assent.
changes: The prohibition in section 88EA on recognising foreign same-sex marriages would be repealed.
The replacement would expressly include unions between a man and another man.
The replacement would also expressly include unions between a woman and another woman.
summary.affected: Same-sex couples whose marriages were solemnised in foreign countries are affected.
